record.title: AMD researchers report a temporally stable one-step diffusion method for global illumination
record.summary: An AMD research group describes a screen-space global-illumination method that uses a one-step latent diffusion model with scene and lighting conditions, plus a Temporal VAE decoder that reuses reprojected prior-frame information to reduce flicker. The authors train on synthetic Blender Cycles interior scenes and report improved PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and FovVideoVDP scores over the compared methods on their test scenes; a compact variant is also shown on real photographs using inverse-rendered inputs. The public technical article does not provide a measured runtime figure, and the research desk did not inspect or reproduce the full ECCV paper results.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: AMD authors describe a one-step latent diffusion model with a Temporal VAE decoder using reprojected previous-frame information to generate geometrically aligned, temporally stable indirect lighting.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On unseen synthetic interior scenes, the authors report better PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and FovVideoVDP results than the compared methods; a compact variant is also shown on real images.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The public AMD article provides no measured runtime or hardware-specific frame-rate result; the method’s real-time feasibility is not established by the inspected source.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of image quality or temporal-stability metrics was performed.
The inspected public summary provides no hardware runtime or frame-rate measurement.

brief.importance_rationale: If the quality and temporal-stability results hold, a one-step diffusion method with a history-aware decoder is a meaningful graphics-rendering design option. Its consequences are currently local to neural global illumination; the available article does not quantify runtime or show a deployed implementation, so it does not justify a higher score.
limitations: AMD is the sole source inspected for the reported performance; no independent reproduction or full paper audit was performed.
The public article gives qualitative and metric-family comparisons but no complete numerical table on the inspected page.
No hardware, inference latency, energy or frame-rate measurement is stated; real-time feasibility is not established.
Training uses synthetic interior scenes; the real-image demonstration uses a compact inverse-rendering-conditioned variant and does not establish broad scene/domain generalization.
brief.summary: An AMD research group describes a screen-space global-illumination method that uses a one-step latent diffusion model with scene and lighting conditions, plus a Temporal VAE decoder that reuses reprojected prior-frame information to reduce flicker. The authors train on synthetic Blender Cycles interior scenes and report improved PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and FovVideoVDP scores over the compared methods on their test scenes; a compact variant is also shown on real photographs using inverse-rendered inputs. The public technical article does not provide a measured runtime figure, and the research desk did not inspect or reproduce the full ECCV paper results.

technical.claimed_result: AMD reports higher PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS and better temporal stability on its unseen synthetic test scenes than the compared methods. It also shows a compact variant on real photographs.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public AMD technical article and its described figures are accessible. No independent reproduction, paper appendix/code inspection, or runtime measurement was performed in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The method treats screen-space indirect lighting as conditional image generation. Scene normals/materials and sparse lighting cues enter a one-step latent diffusion U-Net through T2I-Adapters. A Temporal VAE decoder incorporates the current latent and motion-vector-reprojected prior output, and replaces the frozen VAE decoder at inference.
technical.regime: AMD-reported evaluation trained on synthetic Blender Cycles interior scenes and tested on unseen scenes; a compact inverse-rendering-conditioned model is shown on real photos. The article does not specify measured hardware runtime, frame rate, power, or commercial integration.
technical.strongest_baseline: The article compares against SSGI, BCNN, RGB↔X and DiffusionRenderer, but provides no complete numerical table or matched runtime/quality tradeoff on the inspected page.

brief.title: AMD researchers report a temporally stable one-step diffusion method for global illumination
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced, the work shows a concrete way to combine one-step image generation with temporal history to produce more stable learned indirect lighting. This could affect neural-rendering design, but the public evidence describes synthetic-scene evaluation and does not establish frame-rate feasibility or a product deployment.
